quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on water instead of the road. How can you prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see your car behind the truck. If you drive too close behind or beside a truck, they cannot see you. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Stay farther back than normal.

questions.explanation: Keep at least 3 to 4 seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely is dangerous for both drivers. If the motorcycle falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting the rider. Falls are more likely on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no traffic is coming.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When passing, always signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a curve or hill because few vehicles are coming that way.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
When there is a solid yellow line next to your lane and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
You can only turn right in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When there is a broken yellow line on your side, you can pass if no oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.
Traffic light ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed on vehicles that move slowly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready for red lights, yellow lights, and cross traffic.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows down your reaction time.
Makes you feel less confident.
Gets broken down in your body faster.
Reduces driving mistakes.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes more driving errors.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Low clearance.
Merging traffic.
Prepare to stop.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.
Passing is permitted when it's safe.
Passing is not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted when it's safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line separates lanes going in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street, begin the turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to all drivers on the road. Merge safely when it is possible.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you of a sharp turn ahead and to reduce your speed.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed, signal, and then:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.

questions.explanation: Identify a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Merge into the gap when it is safe. Stay alert and do not expect other drivers to make room.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to conditions that may not be obvious. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery in wet conditions.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep the dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the roadway.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Slow down and be careful.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You should NOT use your horn:

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near a blind pedestrian. It may scare them. Instead, slow down and wait until it is safe to pass.

questions.question: You should honk your horn when you:

options.text: Are traveling through an intersection.
Are passing a bicyclist.
See a child about to run into the street.
Are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: See a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they do not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns of existing or possible dangers.
Alerts drivers to school zones.
Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
Alerts drivers to nearby food and gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of existing or possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions make it harder to concentrate on driving. If you are worried, angry, scared, or sad, it is better to wait before driving.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are generally:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols. You will see them on the sides of the road.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving.

questions.question: This sign shape and color is a ____ sign.

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign means no passing zone.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Travels at the same speed all the time.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver pays attention to other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you more easily.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles often go slower than the speed limit, especially uphill. Be careful when approaching them from behind. When driving uphill with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas
When driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces, even when nearby roads are dry. Bridges also thaw out later than regular roads.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins at the sign where you see it.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?

options.text: The extra distance large vehicles need to stop.
The shorter distance large vehicles need to stop.
The lower noise of large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The extra distance large vehicles need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead. Do not block your view with the truck.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky.
Nothing to worry about.
No more dangerous than other driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers in danger. Focusing on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. If the driver behind you wants to drive faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't block traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when you are driving slower than traffic around you, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and cyclists.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and cyclists.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.explanation: When it is dark and hard to see, increase your following distance. Use headlights to see better. Follow the rules for high beams and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk onto the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more time to stop than passenger cars.
They all have air brakes that help them stop quickly.
They are easier to turn than passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more time to stop than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to stop than other vehicles at the same speed. A passenger car going 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs about 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers that animals, people, or vehicles may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear. Always use your signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: When bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road faster.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Leave more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you may not see.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: When your car breaks down on a highway, move it off the road if possible. Turn on your emergency lights so other drivers can see you are having trouble.

questions.question: When two cars arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control signs, you must yield to a vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know:

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must get out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where it is safe to cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.explanation: A pentagonal sign means you are in or approaching a school zone or school crossing. Watch for children and follow the posted speed limits.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is only used on one-way streets.
You may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if a circular green light appears with it.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.
Under no circumstances.

questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red traffic signal like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.
For any reason.

questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign is a mandatory rule. This sign means never pass other vehicles in this area.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work ahead.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: If you see one deer or moose, you should not expect to see another.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Deer and moose often travel in groups. If one crosses the road, more animals are likely nearby and may cross after it.

questions.question: Since driving involves risk, you should always work to improve your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe when drivers stop trying to improve. Always work to become a better and more aware driver for your safety and others.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is correct because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Can be ticketed.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic congestion.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.explanation: Don't slow down to look at accidents or unusual events. This habit, called "rubbernecking," creates traffic jams.

questions.question: While driving at night, you can use parking lights instead of headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must use headlights when driving at night. Using only parking lights is against the law.
